text:
taylor: Heads up: multiple nodes in us-west2 are failing GPU attach during nightly reclaim. Pattern looks like slow deletes + SMART warnings. Anyone watching storage?

reza: i'm on it. I see a flurry of kernel nvme errors in dmesg on gnode-usw2-118 around 04:03 UTC: `nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, aborting` then `nvme0: media error status=0x2`.

olivia: pulled SMART summary with nvme-cli from that host:
```
$ sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
critical_warning: 0
temperature: 54 C
available_spare: 98%
percentage_used: 32%
data_units_written: 12345
warning_temp_time: 0
nvme_error_count: 14
```
Not huge but error count is creeping. Several nodes show nvme_error_count > 10.

ops: correlate with janitor runs — nightly reclaim job kicks off at 04:00 and it's configured with concurrency=20 for us-west2. That plus active preemptible batch jobs is saturating write IOPS.

taylor: do we have iostat for impacted node?

reza: iostat snapshot from gnode-usw2-118 at 04:05:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1          8.00  410.00  48.00 32768.00   80.00    12.45  29.3   0.90  92.1
```
avgqu-sz 12.45 and %util high.

olivia: also saw overlayfs write amplification on deletes: many small unlink ops cause metadata churn + fsync. Kernel 5.19 overlayfs changes made the unmap path more aggressive which increases syncs.

taylor: So root cause = overlapping reclaim + kernel overlayfs behavior + drives with rising nvme_error_count -> triggers timeouts -> gpu attach fails when underlying image cleanup stalls.

ops: immediate mitigations: 1) reduce reclaim concurrency to 4 in us-west2, 2) throttle reclaim IO to 150MB/s, 3) add a soft-fail fallback so attach will try different node pool if local node is busy.

reza: rolling config change now:
```
rbctl set-config region.us-west2.reclaim.concurrent=4
rbctl set-config region.us-west2.reclaim.io_rate_limit=150MB/s
```
Applying to 50% of nodes (canary) -> done.

oncall-bot: alert suppressed: GPU_ATTACH_TIMEOUTS us-west2 -> 4 recipients notified.

olivia: canary nodes show avgqu-sz down to ~2 within 40s and attach success rate recovers. Good sign.

taylor: medium-term: swap out the 6 worst nvme drives (error_count>12) and mark them for replacement. ops, please open hardware tickets with vendor and schedule replacements during the maintenance window.

ops: opened HW ticket #HW-2026-321 and flagged for priority replacement. Also flagged a follow-up to add `nvme_error_count` to fleet health dashboard.

reza: engineering fix idea: janitor should prefer lazy unlink (defer heavy syncs) and do incremental delete with backoff when nvme_error_count > threshold. I'll draft a change to janitor to read node health and reduce inflight deletes automatically.

olivia: additionally propose we adjust fstrim/scrub schedule so reclaim and scrub don't run in the same 30m window. Put scrub at 02:00 and reclaim at 04:00 in us-west2. That should separate heavy IO windows.

taylor: agree. ops can you make scheduling change and add a guard in job runner to avoid overlapping window.

ops: done — scrub moved to 02:00, reclaim kept at 04:00, added job-runner guard `no_overlap=true`.

reza: PR reference for janitor health-based backoff: https://git.internal/r/redwood/janitor/pulls/489 (draft) — will include `--health-threshold` and `--adaptive-backoff-ms`.

taylor: also add an alarm: if nvme_error_count trend shows +50% week-over-week, auto-schedule fleet replacements and notify oncall.

oncall-bot: scheduled follow-up reminder in 24h for replacement status.

olivia: note on cost: slower reclaim increases ephemeral footprint ~8% while we replace drives. ops, estimate capacity headroom.

ops: we have ~12% spare ephemeral capacity in us-west2; short-term safe. If replacements delayed beyond 72h we'll consider shard-shedding noncritical batch jobs.

taylor: thanks team. Monitor dashboards for next 6 hours and report regressions here. If everything stays green we'll close this thread after replacements scheduled.

reza: ping me if nvme_error_count spikes again, i'll flip on aggressive backoff in janitor.

ops: closing loop in incident system and adding postmortem stub.
